proposals.source: Adam Zsolt Wagner, 'Constructions in combinatorics via neural networks', arXiv:2104.14516, §2.6 (2021)
proposals.quantifiers: Let f_312(n) = max{per(A) : A an n×n 0-1 matrix avoiding the permutation matrix of 312}. Conjecture (record): for every n>=1, f_312(n) = max{per(A) : A in M_n(*,o)}, where M_n(*,o) is the family generated from the 1×1 identity matrix by the two Brualdi–Cao extension operations * and o (direct sum + four prescribed zeros turned to ones, per Figure 12 of the source).
proposals.hypothesis: The conjecture is FALSE: at n=10 the source itself reports the largest permanent obtainable by the recursive operations is 394, while it exhibits 312-avoiding A_10 with per(A_10)=424 (per values 1,2,4,8,16,32,64,120,225,424 for n=1..10; optimality proved only n<=8, so 424 is a valid lower bound for f_312(10) regardless).
proposals.evidence_level: primary-body-read; decisive check NOT yet executed
residuals: Exact definitions of * and o (Figure 12 image) not recovered (guessed image paths 404'd); recorded failure.
Exhaustive max over M_10(*,o) not yet computed by us; the paper's '394' sentence must be confirmed as an exhaustive computation.
Record's references field quotes unrelated §2.4 Collins peak-location prose — mismatch recorded, do not cite it as resolution.
proposals.decisive_next_calculation: Recover Fig. 12 op definitions and Fig. 11 matrices; exhaustively generate M_10(*,o) with dedup (DP over decomposition trees; |S_n| growth bounded by guard) and compute max permanent by Ryser (2^10). Sanity gates: max M_8 must equal 120 and A_8 obtainable; max M_9 >= 225. Then exhibit any 312-avoiding 10×10 matrix with per > max (local search seeded by staircase matrices; avoidance check is polynomial) — that matrix plus Ryser + avoidance verifier is a complete small counterexample certificate.
proposals.certificate_size: small: one 10×10 matrix, avoidance verifier, Ryser permanent, recursive-generation enumerator
proposals.lean_dependency: low-moderate: finite verification; needs decidable matrix/avoidance/permanent definitions, no heavy libraries
proposals.routine_objection: None known: the refutation is NOT a routine adaptation of the already-refuted Brualdi–Cao Fibonacci guess (different claim: extremality of the recursive family, not the specific guessed matrix); the n=10 gap 394<424 is substantive. Prior screen still required (post-2021 work on f_312).

proposals.source: Marek Szykuła, Andrzej Kisielewicz, 'Rainbow Induced Subgraphs in Replication Graphs', arXiv:1201.5340 (2012)
proposals.quantifiers: rho_R(P_n) = minimum number of vertices of a replication graph G of the path P_n such that every proper vertex coloring of G contains a rainbow induced copy of P_n with exactly one vertex in each replication clique. Conjecture (record): for all odd n>=1, rho_R(P_n) = n^2/4 + n^2/16 + 3n/8 + 5/16 if n≡1 (mod 4), and n^2/4 + n^2/16 + 3n/8 + 1/16 if n≡3 (mod 4) (integer-valued; the record's display needs its floor/rounding convention pinned from the source body).
proposals.hypothesis: The odd-n formula is provable by exact dynamic programming over clique-size compositions of n, giving a short constructive certificate (or a small counterexample for the first failing odd n if the search deviates from n<=16 data).
proposals.evidence_level: source-abstract-read; statement completeness 'full' in cached record
residuals: Full body not read (formula rounding convention, definitions); post-2012 literature on rho_R of paths unchecked.
proposals.decisive_next_calculation: Implement exact rho_R(P_n) via composition DP for odd n<=21; compare with conjectured values; if matching, extract the induction; if deviating, exhibit explicit replication graph as counterexample.
proposals.certificate_size: small-to-medium (DP table + induction proof or explicit graph)
proposals.routine_objection: Could be a routine completion of the source's own even-n method — must be checked against the body before crediting; if the odd case needs a genuinely new argument it is substantive.
